subject: Staged acceptance & reservation playbook — proposed MAP and lead-time expectations
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30 09:12 PDT
Subject: Staged acceptance & reservation playbook — proposed MAP and lead-time expectations

Hi Sara / Michael —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I put together a short mutual action plan that ties the evaluation milestones to the GPU reservation windows so we can align procurement and onboarding without blocking your launch. Attached is Acme_MAP_v1.pdf and a rough capacity workbook (capacity_estimate_acme.xlsx). Key highlights: 

- Suggested tranche approach: 2 tranches (pilot then production) with a 6-week gap to allow eval + acceptance.
- Pilot sizing: 8 x A100-equivalent vGPU concurrent slots for 4 weeks of heavy eval; Production baseline: 48 vGPU-equivalent (staggered delivery over 8 weeks).
- Lead times we assume: dedicated/private provisioning ~10–12 weeks once PO is authorized; smaller pilot can be queued in hosted dedicated lanes in ~3 weeks (subject to slot availability).
- Acceptance checkpoints: functional eval (end of week 2), load test (end of week 4), SLA signoff (pre-prod canary week).

Can you confirm the internal procurement window on your side and whether the pilot can start the week of 9/20? If you’re ok we’ll: (1) lock the pilot tranche in our ops booking, (2) begin the eval plan and test data access, (3) schedule an integration walkthrough with your infra team.

Thanks — I left some comments in the MAP doc about fallback routing (cheaper quantized variants) if lead-time slips.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
(kim@redwood.ai)

Attachments: Acme_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP), capacity_estimate_acme.xlsx (workbook)

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear plan and the workbook — that layout is super helpful. High level: procurement is targeting Q3 approvals but we have a flexible PO window if you can secure the pilot tranche in week of 9/20. A couple of asks from our side: 

1) Can you call out a minimal acceptance checklist for the pilot (we want a short list to avoid scope creep)?
2) Are the A100-equivalent numbers coming from a throughput model you ran, or are they conservative buffers?
3) Is there a documented rollback path if production rollout is delayed (we have a hard product deadline Nov 1).

We’ll try to get preliminary signoff from procurement by 9/3 — I’ll know more after our budget sync next week. In the meantime, can Ben or Marissa join a 45-min integration call with our infra lead (cc’d) on 9/7?

—Sara
Head of Platform
Acme AI

Date: 2026-09-01 08:46 PDT
Subject: RE: Staged acceptance & reservation playbook — proposed MAP and lead-time expectations

Sara —

Happy to join the 9/7 integration call. Quick answers inline to help with procurement: 

1) Minimal pilot acceptance checklist (we'll formalize in the MAP doc):
   - End-to-end inference: validated model outputs on 10 canonical prompts
   - Latency target: 95th pct < 220ms for batch size=1 (pilot profile)
   - Throughput: sustained 1k tokens/sec during 30-min load window
   - Data ingress: secure S3 access + VPC egress rules verified
   - Basic security: SOC2 checklist items validated (see SOC2_summary.pdf)

2) Sizing: pilot numbers are conservative and based on the eval traces you shared (we overprovision ~20% to avoid queueing tails). The workbook has a per-model token/sec estimate that produced the A100-equivalent counts. We can tighten after one run of your sample traces.

3) Rollback path: we keep a warm fallback model (quantized variant) in the same region and a cross-region failover policy in the MAP. If production rollout is delayed we will scale down reserved capacity at tranche boundaries and switch traffic to hosted fallbacks. We'll include automatic cost-guard hooks so you don't keep paying for unused tranches.

I’ll draft a short pilot acceptance checklist and post it to the shared MAP before the call.

—Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Team —

Operational notes for the booking desk: if Acme confirms PO by 9/10 we can commit pilot slots for 9/20 start, but production tranche provisioning will need a signed SOW and minimum 10–12 week lead time. Suggested internal milestones:

- 9/07: integration call (Ben + infra)
- 9/10: PO received (ops reserves pilot tranche tentative)
- 9/20: pilot tranche start (4 weeks)
- 10/18: pilot acceptance completed (if all clear, start production provisioning)
- 11/29: minimum production baseline available (assuming 10–12 week provisioning)

Note: if they need a faster production timeline we can discuss partial reservation of preemptible pools for interim capacity (lower SLA) to hit Nov 1; that'll require finance approval for pricing delta.
